note: Styles are design inspiration only. They are not engineering, structural or building-code categories.

styles.name: Contemporary Indian
styles.summary: Clean modern layouts warmed with Indian craft: handloom textiles, brass, cane and a few carefully chosen heirlooms.
signature: Warm neutral walls with one craft-led feature
styles.climate: Adapts well to most Indian climates when paired with breathable fabrics.

styles.name: Traditional South Indian
styles.summary: Courtyard-centred living, carved wooden doors, red oxide or stone floors and brass lamps that glow at dusk.
styles.climate: Courtyards, high ceilings and heavy walls suit hot, humid summers.

styles.name: Chettinad
styles.summary: Grand merchant mansions: patterned Athangudi tiles, egg-plaster walls, Burma teak pillars and saturated earthy colour.
styles.climate: Thick walls and tiled floors stay cool through long hot seasons.

styles.name: Kerala-inspired
styles.summary: Sloping timber ceilings, laterite and lime, polished floors and deep verandahs open to monsoon rain.
styles.climate: Built for heavy monsoon: overhangs, ventilated roofs and quick-drying surfaces.

styles.name: Rajasthani
styles.summary: Jharokha windows, jaali screens, block prints and mirror-work, layered in sandstone pinks and indigo.
styles.climate: Jaali screens and thick stone suit hot, dry climates.

styles.name: Coastal Indian
styles.origin: Konkan, Goa, Malabar and Coromandel coasts
styles.summary: Breezy lime-washed rooms, cane and rattan, oxide floors and the blues and whites of the sea.
styles.climate: Salt-air friendly finishes and cross-ventilation for humid coasts.

styles.name: Bengali heritage
styles.summary: North Kolkata houses with red oxide floors, green louvred shutters, tall doors and four-poster beds.
styles.climate: Tall ceilings and louvres keep humid rooms airy.

styles.name: Modern urban Indian
styles.summary: Smart compact living for city flats: multi-use furniture, hidden storage and calm neutrals with a single bold colour.
styles.climate: Pick moisture-resistant boards for humid metros.

styles.name: Indo-contemporary
styles.summary: A balanced mix of modern forms and Indian motifs: arches, jaali, terrazzo and hand-carved accents.

styles.name: Indian luxury
styles.summary: Rich marbles, silk, carved wood and brass, composed with restraint so materials take centre stage.
styles.climate: Marble floors stay cool; add rugs for composite-climate winters.

styles.name: Minimalist
styles.summary: Fewer, better things: clear surfaces, handle-less storage and light used as a material.
styles.climate: Easy to keep cool and clean in any climate.

styles.name: Japandi
styles.summary: Low, calm furniture in light oak, slatted screens, paper lamps and quiet earthy textiles.
styles.climate: Natural fibres breathe well in humid months.

styles.name: Scandinavian
styles.summary: Bright, simple and cosy: white walls, pale woods, soft textiles and plenty of daylight.
styles.climate: Swap heavy wool for cotton and linen in hot Indian summers.

styles.name: Industrial
styles.summary: Exposed brick and concrete, black metal, reclaimed wood and visible services handled neatly.
styles.climate: Avoid bare metal near the coast unless it is properly treated.

styles.name: Art Deco
styles.summary: Geometric arches, fluted surfaces, terrazzo and brass trims — a style with deep roots on Mumbai's Marine Drive.
styles.climate: Terrazzo and stone suit warm, humid cities.

styles.name: Bohemian
styles.summary: Collected, layered and relaxed: patterned rugs, plants, macramé and travel finds.
styles.climate: Keep layers light and washable in humid regions.
